reviews.title: Persian Gulf aviation GNSS quality anomaly
reviews.reason: The GPSInterference.com report on the Persian Gulf aviation GNSS quality anomaly is based on ADS-B-derived estimates and not confirmed jamming. While the robust Z-score of 0.98 indicates a significant anomaly, the small sample size and median change of 0.7 suggest limited evidence. The lack of corroboration and official alert further reduce the confidence in this anomaly. Therefore, it is recommended to monitor this observation closely.

reviews.title: Strait of Hormuz aviation GNSS quality anomaly
reviews.reason: The GPSInterference.com source provides an ADS-B-derived estimate of a GNSS quality anomaly in the Strait of Hormuz. While the robust Z score of 0.48 indicates a moderate anomaly, the small sample size (38 observations) and median change of -0.75 suggest that this is not a robustly confirmed event. The lack of corroboration and the official alert status further limit the evidence. The anomaly is not considered hostile in nature, and it is recommended to monitor the situation closely.
